name: Digital Signal Processing for Security
description: Ability to apply digital signal processing techniques to RF security analysis tasks. Covers filtering, spectral analysis (FFT/PSD), correlation, signal detection and classification, noise floor characterization, and time-frequency analysis. Enables extraction of intelligence from captured signals beyond basic demodulation.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to digital signal processing concepts

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands basic DSP concepts including sampling, filtering, and frequency-domain representation
evidence: Can explain Fourier transforms, filtering, and aliasing at a conceptual level
Completed introductory DSP training or equivalent coursework
Understands the role of DSP in RF signal analysis

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Applies standard DSP techniques using existing tools and scripts under supervision
evidence: Applied FFT-based spectral analysis to captured signals using Python/NumPy or GNU Radio
Designed and applied basic FIR/IIR filters to isolate signals of interest under guidance
Used spectrogram/waterfall analysis to characterize signal timing patterns

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently applies DSP techniques to extract information from complex signal captures
evidence: Independently characterized signal parameters (bandwidth, symbol rate, periodicity) using DSP techniques
Applied correlation and matched filtering for signal detection in noisy captures
Implemented custom DSP processing chains for lab analysis tasks
Documented DSP processing parameters and results for reproducibility

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Develops advanced DSP analysis pipelines; applies statistical signal processing to challenging problems
evidence: Developed automated signal classification pipelines using statistical or ML-based approaches
Applied advanced techniques (cyclostationary analysis, wavelet transforms, blind source separation) to real captures
Built reusable DSP analysis tools for the lab
Mentors junior analysts on DSP technique selection and application

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines lab DSP methodology; develops novel analysis techniques; recognized signal processing authority
evidence: Published research on DSP techniques for security signal analysis
Designed the lab's standard DSP processing and analysis toolkit
Developed novel signal detection or classification methods applied in lab operations
Trains teams on DSP fundamentals and advanced techniques

assessment_methods.description: Given a raw IQ capture containing multiple overlapping signals, isolate and characterize each signal using DSP techniques
Design a processing chain to detect and extract a weak signal of interest from a capture with strong adjacent-channel interference
